nodes.name: Self-catalytic NiFe Nanoreactor Formation
nodes.procedure: Four different solutions, A (nickel sulfate hexahydrate and ferrous sulfate heptahydrate aqueous solution), B (NaOH aqueous solution), C (citric acid monohydrate aqueous solution), and D (sodium hypophosphite aqueous solution), were prepared at the beginning. Then, under relatively mild conditions, the four solutions were sequentially added to a reaction vessel, and a precipitate will be acquired after centrifuge. Among those steps, Ni-Fe hydroxide nanospheres will be formed after adding solution B, and solution C can help to stabilize the spheres. When solution D was added, the Ni-Fe hydroxide nanospheres were transformed to NiO and Fe3O4 by sodium hypophosphite under the catalytic function of Ni-Fe hydroxide itself (noted as self-catalysis), which grew outward to form synapses. Those synapses are slowly intertwined to form a grid surrounding the NiFe hydroxide. When the grid becomes thicker, many channels are formed inside it, and the inner NiFe hydroxide core is furtherly reduced. Until the NiFe hydroxide is exhausted, the gaps in the outer mesh are filled, forming a hollow sphere.

nodes.procedure: Then, the fillers in the channels were washed away with HNO3 (Solution E), thus obtaining a hollow NiFe amorphous nanoreactor with multiple channels.
